executive_assessment.text: Dikhil, Obock and Tadjourah pastoral rainfall deficits and dated camp/rural food-security estimates give differentiated local vulnerability, with non-climate drivers preserved.
Dikhil's service constraints and planned refugee-inclusive investments add FCV-relevant capacity context. UNDP's water/rangeland targets and early-warning needs remain design evidence.

geographic_notes.text: The May–June 2025 IPC analysis estimates Phase 3+ food insecurity among 30% of analyzed populations in Dikhil Rural and Obock Rural and 25% in Tadjourah Rural.

The same May–June 2025 IPC table estimates Phase 3+ rates of 50% in Markazi and 30% in Ali Addeh and Holl-Holl camps; it lists livelihood, purchasing-power and assistance constraints alongside climate shocks in some zones.
Source dated 2025-06-24 reports: IPC reported 104,000 food-assistance recipients nationally, substantial coverage in supported villages/camps, and an urban coverage gap.

Source dated 2025-07-09 reports: In inland pastoral areas of Dikhil, Obock and Tadjourah, March–May rainfall was about 50% below average; the brief says deficits impaired rangeland regeneration and pasture and water availability, worsening livestock body condition.
Source dated 2025-02-21 reports: The February 2025 PAD lists refugees/asylum seekers in Obock, Holl-Holl, Ali Addeh and Djibouti-Ville; conflict and disasters are separate movement contexts.
Source dated 2025-02-21 reports: The PAD describes Dikhil's weak services, unemployment and aridity, with migration and climate vulnerability adding pressures.
The February 2025 appraisal proposes basic services, safety nets and resilient drainage/water investments in high-hazard, vulnerable locations, including refugee-hosting areas.

Source dated not stated reports: UNDP lists a six-year project under implementation for 100,000 people, half women, in Ali Sabieh, Dikhil, Tadjourah and Obock. Planned activities include local early warning, water and rangeland management, and climate-resilient livelihoods.

Source dated not stated reports: The project page identifies gaps in technical/government capacity for water management and community landscape management, plus limited local and regional flood/drought early warning; these are stated constraints motivating the project.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 20 of 20 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The revised 2025 NDC is available in French; paraphrases were made from the French text, and local climate projections are not disaggregated by region in the cited passages.
The World Bank CCDR full report and model assumptions were not retrieved; its summary does not provide uncertainty ranges for the stated urban and livelihood estimates.
The NDC reports a risk of rural livelihood-driven movement toward urban peripheries, but does not establish conflict, violence, or measured migration outcomes.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
No inspected source explicitly attributes armed conflict or violence in Djibouti to climate hazards; the PAD names conflict and climate-disaster displacement as separate contexts.

The full Djibouti Country Climate and Development Report could not be read because the browser parser rejected its large PDF and a local retrieval attempt did not complete; claims rely on other official full-text sources.
The IPC projection and UNDP/WB activities are conditional or planned, not observed outcomes; IPC identifies assistance reductions and low purchasing power as important non-climate drivers.
No inspected source established that insecurity constrained adaptation delivery or disaster response; this is recorded as a search gap rather than inferred from displacement or service pressure.

Main checked the publicly released PAD cover: it expressly authorizes public availability before Board consideration despite its standard official-use header. It is retained as dated appraisal evidence, not a Board outcome or implementation result.
Named rural and camp rates are May–June 2025 IPC estimates. Service pressure does not itself establish host–refugee violence or a climate-caused migration mechanism.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
